comment: Closed registry of refusal-event kinds (remediation plan Phase 0.1). Every refusal exit in the harness writes exactly one events.jsonl row whose kind is listed here. Additions are data-file diffs visible in git; runtime code never invents a kind. The writer maps any unregistered kind to refusal-unregistered so a refusal signal is never swallowed by a registry gap. Each kind carries its signal/bound class (round-5 F-6): the registry OWNS a kind's NO-relevance; acceptance_baseline.json only cites it, and check_acceptance refuses a contradiction — the boolean that can disarm the deadline is never an unpinned baseline value.

refusal-dispatch.description: dispatch_lane.sh fail(): lane dispatch refused before launch

refusal-phase1-gate.description: phase1_gate.sh gate G: artifact adequacy gate refused; lanes must not launch

refusal-promote.description: promote.sh fail-closed exit: refused control, no verdict rendered

refusal-endgame.description: endgame.sh refusal exit: endgame could not complete its judgment

refusal-unregistered.description: a refusal path supplied a kind absent from this registry; the attempted kind is recorded in detail

construction-no-candidate.description: a host-counted lane dispatch ended without a reviewable candidate (plan 0.4b): itself a NO-relevant signal — it fires the deadline and cannot burn unbounded wall-clock invisible to the instrument; RESERVED — no emitter is wired yet (the lane-completion accounting in dispatch_lane.sh wires it; round-6 6-10 corrected this description, which previously claimed an emitter that did not exist)

refusal-tmux-lane.description: tmux_lane.sh refuse(): a tmux author lane launch or qualification probe refused before the agent started (sign-in preflight, missing spend cap, unqualified metered model, budget, testing standard, CLI contract, or a lane with no watcher)

refusal-lane-stall.description: watchdog.py lane: the lane made no commit within its stall window after the read allowance, so the watcher stopped it and woke the operator

refusal-lane-cap.description: watchdog.py lane: the lane reached its spend cap (declared rate x wall clock) or wall-clock cap and the watcher stopped it; a declared bound, never an instrument-rewarded signal
